topology: Four area0 routers share 10.0.123.0/24 through SW1. R1 priority200 is DR, R2 priority100 is BDR and R3/R4 priority0 are DROTHERs. A separate R3–R4 Gi0/2 primary joins 10.0.34.0/30. PC1 is behind R3, PC2 behind R2 and HTTP SRV1 behind R4. Primary cost5 plus LAN1 gives service cost6; shared cost10 plus LAN1 gives backup/control cost11. Initially the primary is broadcast with both priorities0, so it cannot elect a DR or exchange its database.
implemented: Twenty-first ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry, independent practice/reference documents, eight-row interface/address/role plan, detailed staged guide, ordinary IOS/Windows commands and current-domain/path/query permalinks. Existing UI, artwork, offline delivery and terminal styles are preserved.

Initial diagnosis requires actual three-request/three-reply exchanges in four directions: PC1/server and PC2/server, both ways. Initial PC1 traffic must cross the shared switch directly between DROTHERs; the DR must not become an obligatory data-forwarding hop. Shared 2-Way between DROTHERs is normal, whereas no eligible primary DR prevents primary Full adjacency.

Repair both primary interfaces to point-to-point. Live checks require intended interface policies, shared DR/BDR and ten directed Full plus two directed 2-Way relationships, two primary Full relationships without primary DR/BDR, four received router LSAs and shared network advertisement, exact AD110 costs6/11 with next hops and CEF egresses, HTTP service and saved R1–R4 configs.

Observed fresh four-way ICMP requires accepted requests, parent-linked replies and intended router/switch egresses after configuration/route epochs. HTTP requires an actually completed TCP-backed200 response and expected body. Configuration-only changes, insufficient directions, two replies, stale traffic, static shortcuts and missing control delivery cannot earn the corresponding proof.

A one-sided point-to-multipoint change exposes default30/120 versus point-to-point10/40 mismatch and working shared fallback. An operational broadcast comparison uses primary priority1, DR/BDR, Full adjacency and an additional network advertisement before restoring P2P. The guide explicitly avoids claiming every network-type mismatch prevents Full.

NBMA and point-to-multipoint nonbroadcast each require observed missing-static-neighbor fallback and four delivered directions, followed by reciprocal router-level neighbor configuration, actual unicast control delivery and cost6 forwarding. NBMA elects DR/BDR; point-to-multipoint does not. Multicast point-to-multipoint uses default30/120, actual multicast control delivery and Full without a primary DR/BDR. Every exercise ends with removal of temporary neighbors, restoration of P2P/priority0 and fresh four-way proof.

Point-to-point priority255 leaves the primary Full without DR/BDR; the exercise restores priority0 and proves fresh traffic. Six controlled exercises plus diagnosis, traffic and HTTP yield nine historical checks; seven live checks remain live. Practice starts0/16, diagnosis1/16, repaired baseline10/16 and full16/16. Completed reference provides seven live checks only. YAML retains earned history while clearing runtime and a fresh attempt starts over.

Fixed an engine discovery/SPF conflation: no-DR 2-Way relationships were omitted from the Hello candidate graph, so actual received Hellos could not maintain the peer. They now remain discovery candidates while only received LSAs supply SPF links. A regression advances300 simulated seconds, checks fresh received Hellos and persistent2WAY, forbids a primary network advertisement/shortcut and proves shared cost11 traffic.
Question-mark and Tab now include the optional non-broadcast suffix after ip ospf network point-to-multipoint, matching the already implemented parser form.
scope: IOS OSPFv2 network-type discovery, timers, adjacency roles and routed forwarding using existing simulated logical control/data-plane delivery. Router LSAs are received logical records; Type-2 show output is projected from received topology, not a native wire-format Type-2 encoder. Unicast/multicast checks inspect actual OSPF frames and endpoints, not a decoded wire Hello subtype. No fresh CML capture, Frame Relay/PVC implementation, P2MP transit-host-/32 route semantics, exhaustive mismatch behavior or complete RFC state/timing/wire interoperability is claimed.
